The stock market closed lower on Monday after a volatile session that saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 Index both fall more than 1%. The Nasdaq Composite Index was the only major index to finish in positive territory, rising 0.2%.

The session was marked by a lack of clear direction, with stocks moving between gains and losses throughout the day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 300 points at one point, but managed to recoup some of its losses to close down 1.2%. The S&P 500 Index fell 1.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite Index rose 0.2%.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index was boosted by gains in Apple Inc., Amazon.com Inc., and Microsoft Corp. These companies all reported strong earnings last week, which helped to offset losses in other sectors.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was weighed down by losses in Caterpillar Inc., Chevron Corp., and Boeing Co. These companies all have significant exposure to the global economy, which has been slowing down in recent months.

The S&P 500 Index was dragged down by losses in financial stocks. Bank of America Corp., Citigroup Inc., and JPMorgan Chase & Co. all fell more than 1%.

The overall trend for the stock market is uncertain. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 Index have both been in a downtrend since the beginning of the year, while the Nasdaq Composite Index has been in a more sideways trend. The market is likely to remain volatile in the near term, as investors try to gauge the impact of the slowing global economy and the upcoming U.S. presidential election.
